question.worked_solution:
The "square of a sum" formula states that

$$
{x}^{2}+2ax+{a}^{2}=(x+a)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
16x+64+{x}^{2}={x}^{2}+16x+64.
$$

First, we write the constant term as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+16x+{8}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2\cdot 8x+{8}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of sum formula with $a=8.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+8)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
